title: Jesus, the Essenes, sacrifice and meat
subtitle: Debate prep: the strongest honest case for the resolution, where it will be attacked, and what not to say.

it: 3 · THE MOVEMENT AFTER HIM: NO ALTAR, NO MEAT
WHAT THEY WILL SAY · AND THE ANSWER

THE RESOLUTION

Jesus belonged to an Essene group that rejected animal sacrifice and did not eat meat.

HOW WE HOLD IT: three claims, and they are not equally strong.

1. SACRIFICE. Our strongest ground, and it is red text about Jesus himself: Hosea quoted twice, the Temple action, Mark 12:33-34.

2. MEAT. Strong for the movement after him (James, the Nazarenes, the Ebionites), and every witness is hostile or disinterested. For the Essenes themselves it rests on one late writer, Porphyry. Argue the Nazarene movement, not the Essene menu.

3. BELONGING. Strong as a stream, weak as a membership card. Claim the stream.

The sentence that holds every word: the movement that claimed succession from Jesus through his brother James rejected sacrifice and abstained from flesh, and we know it from the people who were trying to discredit it.

A vocabulary found nowhere in the Hebrew Bible ("spirit of truth", "children of light") runs all through the gospels. Same proof text, same wilderness, same immersion. That is the stream.

Don't claim a membership card: he ate with sinners and drank wine, and reform movements criticize their parent hardest.

This half is red text about Jesus himself. He threw Hosea 6:6 at the men running the cult, twice. He stopped the Temple traffic quoting the one chapter where God denies commanding burnt offerings, and Mark 11:18 says that is when they sought to destroy him.

Every witness here was hostile or disinterested, which is why it holds. By 314, Canon 14 of Ancyra had to order clergy who abstained from flesh to at least taste it.

Concede the asymmetry out loud: this is evidence about the movement, not about what was on Jesus's plate.

DR. PETE (Orthodox), Kam's video 04: "He kept Passover, so he ate the lamb."

No gospel narrates him eating lamb. All three Synoptics narrate bread and wine at the sacrificial meal.

"He ate broiled fish. Q calls him a glutton."

That lands on belonging, not on the movement's practice. A movement's rule and its founder's table are different records, and the gospels were never a diet log.

JOHN DAVIS, episode 026: "The Theosophical Society invented the vegetarian Jesus."

Concede what is true first: the Essene Gospel of Peace is a modern book. Then the pre-modern witnesses: James in Hegesippus (2nd century), the Ebionites in Epiphanius (4th), Ancyra (314). Still OPEN in the objections bank, brief D.

✗ "Qumran was anti-sacrifice."
The Temple Scroll prescribes it and 4QMMT is about doing it correctly. Boycott, not abolition.

✗ "Four historians confirm Essene vegetarianism."
One does: Porphyry, 3rd century, paraphrasing Josephus. Pliny says nothing about diet.

✗ Josephus on the Essenes not sacrificing (Antiquities 18.1.5).
The sentence turns on a disputed negative.

✗ The Essene Gospel of Peace as an ancient text.
It is Szekely's, a twentieth-century book.

✗ "I have no desire to eat the flesh of this Passover" as Jesus's words.
It is Epiphanius quoting the Ebionites' version of Luke 22:15: evidence of the movement, not of Jesus.
